newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Roskhleboprodukt plans Canada grain talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Roskhleboprodukt plans Canada grain talks.

text.p: Russia's AO Roskhleboprodukt will conduct grain buying talks with Canada on Thursday, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Zaveryukha said on Wednesday.
"Tomorrow, our non-government commercial structure, Roskhleboprodukt, will conduct talks on that topic with its Canadian counterpart," Zaveryukha, in charge of Russian agriculture, told reporters.
"There could be buys of Canadian grain for our Far East, to where it is more profitable to bring grain across the ocean than pay high railroad tariffs to send it overland."
Zaveryukha, speaking during a Candian-Russian economic summit, declined to say what amount or type of grain would be discussed.
"The regions themselves and commercial structures -- not government structures -- will determine the volume of (grain) buying," he said.
A Canadian Wheat Board representative present at the summit declined to comment.
Zaveryukha said Russia would buy grain for the Far East where it got the best deal, and mentioned Canada, Australia and the U.S. as possible sources.
The Canadian Wheat Board is Roskhleboprodukt's likely counterpart in grain buying talks, but Zaveryukha did not mention the board by name.
